key_insight: Wind shear and veer can lower actuator-disk power efficiency by over 20% because they change both the effective inflow geometry and the turbine’s induction/aerodynamics.
engineering_relevance: Power prediction and turbine-control models should account for shear- and veer-driven induction effects, not just rotor-equivalent wind speed, to improve performance estimates in realistic atmospheric boundary layers.
method: Concurrent-precursor large-eddy simulations (LES) of an actuator disk in stratified ABL conditions
Controlled inflow LES with shear and veer varied independently
Decomposition of losses into geometric and inductive contributions
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the simulations reproduce efficiency losses exceeding 20% and show that shear and veer effects approximately linearly superimpose.
watch_item: The conclusions are based on actuator-disk LES and controlled idealized inflow cases, so translating them directly to full rotor geometry and farm-scale operation will need additional validation.
paper_title: Influence of wind shear and veer on power, thrust, and induction of an actuator disk
